title: "Stress & Strain: The 1D Picture"
---

## The stress-strain curve

A typical uniaxial stress-strain response shows a linear elastic region up to a
**yield point**, followed by strain hardening to the **ultimate tensile strength (UTS)**,
then softening (necking) to **fracture**.

![](stress_strain_curve.png){width=70%}

Note: this is a schematic, not-to-scale illustration — real elastic strains are far
smaller relative to the plastic strain range than shown here.

## Key relations

$$
\sigma = E\varepsilon \qquad (\varepsilon \le \varepsilon_y)
$$

$$
\sigma_y = E\,\varepsilon_y
$$
